trades.name: Cash convergence: butter and dry whey
trades.thesis: Butter and whey futures settle on USDA's monthly average of the weekly plant survey, which follows CME spot with a 1-2 week lag. When spot has moved and the futures have not, the futures have to converge toward the spot-based estimate by settlement.
trades.entry: On Wednesday, after the 11:00 am CT USDA weekly report (NDPSR) and the CME spot session: for each butter and whey contract up to 2 months out, if the desk's estimate of the settlement is above the futures by more than the round-trip cost (shown below), buy one lot; if below, sell one. Enter near the settlement price.
trades.exit: Re-check every Wednesday. Close when the estimate-vs-futures gap shrinks below the round-trip cost or flips sign, or hold to final settlement (the USDA announcement in the first days of the following month; the contract stops trading the day before).
trades.risk: No stop was used in the test. Size so the historical worst drawdown is tolerable; a large unexpected move in CME spot during the month is the main risk, so it falls as more weeks are published.

trades.name: Cash convergence confirmed by the futures trend (all six)
trades.thesis: Same convergence logic across all six contracts, but only when the futures have already moved the same way over the last 4 weeks. Fewer trades, better return per unit of drawdown than the plain version.
trades.entry: Wednesday, after the USDA weekly report: estimate above futures by more than the cost AND the contract up at least the cost over the last 4 weeks (or the mirror for shorts). Contracts up to 2 months out.
trades.exit: Wednesday re-check: close if either condition fails, or hold to settlement.
trades.risk: Class III and cheese are efficiently priced on their own; the trend filter is what keeps them from losing.

trades.name: Spot-month lock-in (lowest risk)
trades.thesis: Once the first weekly prints of the month are published, part of the monthly average is locked and the rest follows spot already seen. The remaining risk is small, so this is the closest to a true arbitrage; edges are small and frequent.
trades.entry: From the 8th of the month: current-month contract only, all six; trade the direction of the estimate-vs-futures gap when it exceeds the round-trip cost.
trades.exit: Hold to final settlement, or close if the gap falls below cost at a Wednesday check.
trades.risk: Liquidity in the expiring month is thin; work orders near the settlement.

trades.name: 4-week futures trend (all six, up to 5 months out)
trades.thesis: Dairy settlement prices are averages of slow-moving survey prices, so moves persist for weeks; futures inherit part of that persistence.
trades.entry: Weekly (Wednesday): hold one lot per contract month in the direction of its change over the last 4 weeks, when that change is larger than the round-trip cost.
trades.exit: Flip or flatten when the 4-week change reverses or falls below the cost at the weekly check.
trades.risk: Largest drawdowns of all the ideas (many positions); run it smaller than the convergence trades.

trades.name: Breakout with trailing stop: Butter
trades.thesis: Right less than half the time, but stops keep losers small while the occasional long dairy trend runs; small drawdowns per lot.
trades.entry: Daily on the contract about 2 months out (2026-12): buy when it settles above its 20-day high (now 144.700); sell when it settles below its 20-day low (now 131.525).
trades.exit: Long: close on a settle below the 10-day low or the trailing stop (2x the 20-day average daily move below the best close). Short: the mirror. Also close 10 days before the USDA announcement.
trades.risk: Average daily move 1.755 ¢/lb; stop distance about 3.510.
track: Daily settlement vs the 20-day high/low and the stop (this page, nightly)

trades.name: Formula arbitrage: Class III / IV vs component futures
trades.thesis: Class III is a fixed formula of the cheese, butter and whey averages (Class IV: butter and nonfat); the class contract and its components settle on the same USDA numbers, so a price gap between them must close by expiry.
trades.entry: When the Class futures differ from the price implied by the component futures of the same month by more than $0.20/cwt: sell the dear side, buy the cheap side in the hedge ratio shown (per 10 Class contracts).
trades.exit: Hold to settlement, or close when the gap is back under about $0.05.
trades.risk: Four thin legs; quotes can be stale, so check live bids and offers before acting.
